note: Approximate values for visualisation. Deep-time anchors are rounded readings of published compilations; see sources per series and DECISIONS.md.

temperature.label: Global mean surface temperature
sources: Judd, E.J. et al. (2024) A 485-million-year history of Earth's surface temperature. Science 385, eadk3705 (PhanDA)
Scotese, C.R. et al. (2021) Phanerozoic paleotemperatures. Earth-Science Reviews 215, 103503
Westerhold, T. et al. (2020) An astronomically dated record of Earth's climate (CENOGRID). Science 369, 1383
Osman, M.B. et al. (2021) Globally resolved surface temperatures since the Last Glacial Maximum. Nature 599, 239
Precambrian: qualitative ranges from Hoffman et al. (2017) Snowball Earth climate dynamics, Sci. Adv. 3, e1600983; Catling & Zahnle (2020) Sci. Adv. 6, eaax1420
Future: Farnsworth, A. et al. (2023) Climate extremes likely to drive land mammal extinction during next supercontinent assembly. Nat. Geosci. 16, 901
Lisiecki, L.E. & Raymo, M.E. (2005) A Pliocene-Pleistocene stack of 57 globally distributed benthic δ18O records. Paleoceanography 20, PA1003 (scaled to GMST)

co2.label: Atmospheric CO₂
sources: Bereiter, B. et al. (2015) Revision of the EPICA Dome C CO2 record from 800 to 600 kyr before present. GRL 42, 542 (0–800 ka)
The Cenozoic CO2 Proxy Integration Project (CenCO2PIP) Consortium (2023) Toward a Cenozoic history of atmospheric CO2. Science 382, eadi5177
Foster, G.L., Royer, D.L. & Lunt, D.J. (2017) Future climate forcing potentially without precedent in the last 420 million years. Nat. Commun. 8, 14845
Royer, D.L. (2014) Atmospheric CO2 and O2 during the Phanerozoic: tools, patterns and impacts. Treatise on Geochemistry 6, 251
Precambrian: Catling & Zahnle (2020) The Archean atmosphere. Sci. Adv. 6, eaax1420; Kanzaki & Murakami (2015) GCA 159, 190
Today: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory annual mean (2024)

oxygen.label: Atmospheric O₂
sources: Lyons, T.W., Reinhard, C.T. & Planavsky, N.J. (2014) The rise of oxygen in Earth's early ocean and atmosphere. Nature 506, 307
Krause, A.J. et al. (2018) Stepwise oxygenation of the Paleozoic atmosphere. Nat. Commun. 9, 4081
Berner, R.A. (2009) Phanerozoic atmospheric oxygen: new results using the GEOCARBSULF model. Am. J. Sci. 309, 603
Poulton, S.W. et al. (2021) A 200-million-year delay in permanent atmospheric oxygenation. Nature 592, 232

seaLevel.label: Global sea level relative to today
sources: Lambeck, K. et al. (2014) Sea level and global ice volumes from the Last Glacial Maximum to the Holocene. PNAS 111, 15296 (0–21 ka)
Spratt, R.M. & Lisiecki, L.E. (2016) A Late Pleistocene sea level stack. Clim. Past 12, 1079 (21–800 ka)
Miller, K.G. et al. (2020) Cenozoic sea-level and cryospheric evolution from deep-sea geochemical and continental margin records. Sci. Adv. 6, eaaz1346
Haq, B.U. (2014) Cretaceous eustasy revisited. Global Planet. Change 113, 44; Haq (2018) Jurassic/Triassic sea-level variations
Haq, B.U. & Schutter, S.R. (2008) A chronology of Paleozoic sea-level changes. Science 322, 64
Note: before ~5 Ma the PaleoDEM coastlines already include the paleo sea level; this curve is shown for information

dayLength.label: Length of day
sources: de Winter, N.J. et al. (2020) Subdaily-scale chemical variability in a Torreites rudist shell. Paleoceanogr. Paleoclimatol. 35, e2019PA003723 (70 Ma: 23.5 h)
Wells, J.W. (1963) Coral growth and geochronometry. Nature 197, 948 (Devonian ≈ 400 days/yr)
Williams, G.E. (2000) Geological constraints on the Precambrian history of Earth's rotation and the Moon's orbit. Rev. Geophys. 38, 37 (620 Ma: 21.9 h)
Meyers, S.R. & Malinverno, A. (2018) Proterozoic Milankovitch cycles and the history of the solar system. PNAS 115, 6363 (1.4 Ga: 18.7 h)
Lantink, M.L. et al. (2022) Milankovitch cycles in banded iron formations constrain the Earth–Moon system 2.46 billion years ago. PNAS 119, e2117146119 (16.9 h)
Mitchell, R.N. & Kirscher, U. (2023) Mid-Proterozoic day length stalled by tidal resonance. Nat. Geosci. 16, 567
Eulenfeld, T. & Heubeck, C. (2023) Constraints on Moon's orbit 3.2 billion years ago from tidal bundle data. JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007466
Earliest values after the Moon-forming impact are speculative (Canup 2004; Ćuk & Stewart 2012)

moonDistance.label: Earth–Moon distance
sources: Lunar Laser Ranging: present recession 3.8 cm/yr (Williams & Boggs 2016)
Williams (2000), Meyers & Malinverno (2018), Lantink et al. (2022), Eulenfeld & Heubeck (2023) — as for day length
Initial distance of a few Earth radii after the giant impact is speculative (Canup 2004)

sources: Judd et al. (2024); Evans, D. et al. (2018) PNAS 115, 1174; hothouse climates have weaker gradients
Som, S.M. et al. (2016) Earth's air pressure 2.7 billion years ago constrained to less than half of modern levels. Nat. Geosci. 9, 448
Arney, G. et al. (2016) The pale orange dot: the spectrum and habitability of hazy Archean Earth. Astrobiology 16, 873
Zerkle, A.L. et al. (2012) A bistable organic-rich atmosphere on the Neoarchaean Earth. Nat. Geosci. 5, 359
Segura, A. et al. (2003) Ozone concentrations and ultraviolet fluxes on Earth-like planets. Astrobiology 3, 689
Zahnle, K. et al. (2010) Earth's earliest atmospheres. Cold Spring Harb. Perspect. Biol. 2, a004895
